title: Normalized continuous-set Kan comparison and evaluation on contractible affines
statement:
Use compatible universes and small skeletons [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a profinite $S$ let $a_X(S)=X[S]$ and $r_{X,S}:|X[S]|\to S$ be the relative test object and label projection specified in [lem-sfb-relative-profinite-test-labels]. Let $p_X^*=\pi_X^{-1}a^*$ be the specified set-valued inverse image [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback], where $\pi_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. For any sheaf $H$ of sets on profinite spaces, put $P_H=\operatorname{Lan}_{a_X^{op}}H$. There is a natural isomorphism $P_H^\#\cong p_X^*H$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] that identifies the Kan/sheafification adjunction with the composite adjunction defining $p_X^*$; its right adjoint is $G\mapsto(S\mapsto G(X[S]))$. Let $D$ be any topological space and suppose $\underline D(S)=C(S,D)$ and $F_{D,X}(U)=C(|U|,D)$ [def-sfb-continuous-set-presheaf] are sheaves. There is a unique morphism $\sigma_{D,X}:p_X^*\underline D\to F_{D,X}$ whose image under this adjunction sends every $b\in C(S,D)$ to $b\circ r_{X,S}$. Its presheaf adjunct on the Kan colimit is
$$[(S,\phi:U\to X[S]),b]\longmapsto b\circ r_{X,S}\circ|\phi|.$$
If $D$ is Hausdorff and totally disconnected and $U$ is a weakly contractible affine object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (evaluation at $U$ sends epimorphisms of set sheaves to surjections), put $T=\pi_0(|U|)$. Every Kan-colimit class has a representative $[(T,\phi_U),c]$, where $r_{X,T}|\phi_U|=q_U$, and the displayed map sends it to $c q_U$. This map is bijective, and its factorization through the canonical sheafification map $P_{\underline D}(U)\to P_{\underline D}^\#(U)$ identifies it with $\sigma_{D,X}(U)$; that sheafification map and $\sigma_{D,X}(U)$ are bijective. All these identifications use the displayed normalization, not an unspecified section isomorphism.

source.place: Example 3.1, p.6; adjunction expansion using Stacks Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq to the Kan/sheafification adjunction and the specified composite adjunction. Its homEquiv_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app equation, followed by homEquiv_naturality_right and homEquiv_unit, proves the displayed normalization for every morphism f. The pointwise left Kan extension cocone is a colimit; Types.jointly_surjective_of_isColimit gives representatives using precisely its actual legs.

The relative label theorem identifies its r with the specified continuousSetRelativeTestProjection pointwise. Its label naturality makes b maps to b composed with r into a sheaf morphism theta from the continuous-function profinite sheaf to the common right adjoint. Invert the specified composite hom equivalence to obtain sigma; injectivity of that equivalence proves uniqueness. Define alpha by the displayed canonical-unit factorization. Expand the restricted Kan/sheafification hom equivalence and use its equality with the composite hom equivalence. The result says lanUnit followed by the whiskered alpha equals theta. Evaluating and using alpha naturality gives the required formula on every leg.

source.place: Tag 00VE (lemma-adjoints-u), explicit converse construction; Tag 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint). HRS Example 3.1, p.6, fixes the continuous-function normalization.

proof.text: For affine U use the terminal-label clause of the relative test label theorem to obtain phi_U with label q_U. Mathlib continuousMapPresheafEquivOfTotallyDisconnectedSpace factors each continuous label into a profinite S through the actual component quotient. The label factorization clause gives phi equals phi_U followed by X[g]. Naturality of lanUnit gives the Kan relation taking b on this leg to b composed with g on the phi_U leg. Pointwise Kan joint surjectivity therefore proves the required normal representatives. The affine connected-component quotient has its existing profinite instances.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12 and Lemma 4.2.13(1), p.30, factorization through connected components and the inverse-image Kan calculation.

proof.text: Mathlib continuousMapPresheafEquivOfTotallyDisconnectedSpace has inverse exactly c maps to c composed with q_U. Its bijectivity gives the component factorization bijection without additional geometric hypotheses. The leg formula and the phi_U label equation compute alpha on every normal representative. For surjectivity lift each continuous function by this equivalence. For injectivity replace two elements with normal representatives and apply injectivity of precomposition with q_U. No inhabitance is assumed, so empty schemes and empty coefficients are included.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12 and the normal-representative calculation in the proof of Lemma 4.2.13(1), p.30.

proof.text: Apply the existing pro-etale sheafification-on-weakly-contractible-sections lemma with the set sheaf $F=\underline D$. Its presheaf is precisely $P_{\underline D}$, since it uses the same inverse-limit relative test objects, identified in step 1. It states that the canonical unit $\eta_U:P_{\underline D}(U)\to P_{\underline D}^\#(U)$ is bijective, under exactly the present meaning of weak contractibility (surjectivity on sections for every set-sheaf epimorphism). By step 3, $\alpha_U=\sigma_{D,X}(U)e_{\underline D}(U)\eta_U$. Hence, after the normalized identification $e$, the factorization is $\sigma_{D,X}(U)=\alpha_U\eta_U^{-1}$. Steps 2 and 5 and the cited unit bijectivity prove that $\sigma_{D,X}(U)$ is bijective, with the required normalization throughout.
